statement: ▶ Question 2. For which k and t is the family of Pt -free minimal Wk -obstructions finite?
context: Minimal obstructions. Recall that by Theorem 2 and Theorem 3, the only connected graphs F for which we can hope for a finite family of F -free minimal Wk -obstructions are paths. This leads to the following question. ▶ Question 2. For which k and t is the family of Pt -free minimal Wk -obstructions finite? Let us point out that for all k, the number of P4 -free minimal Wk -obstructions is finite. Indeed, P4 -free graphs are perfect. Thus if G is P4 -free and does not contain K4 , then G is 3-colorable (and thus it admits a homomorphism to Wk ). On the other hand, K4 is a minimal graph that does not admit a homomorphism to Wk . Concluding, K4 is the only P4 -free (even P3 -free) Wk -obstruction. On the negative side, recall that there exists an infinite family of P7 -free 4-vertex-critical graphs [9]. An inspection of this family shows that these graphs are minimal Wk -obstructions for every odd k ⩾ 5. Note that for each such graph G, the fact that an induced subgraph G′ of G has a proper 3-coloring implies that G′ has a homomorphism to Wk . However, it still needs to be verified that G itself does not admit a homomorphism to Wk .
